# SPEC: src/relay/digest-evidence-fixes.test.ts
# UNSCORED DIAGNOSTIC MISSION 4, CANDIDATE C: two latent defects in two independent pure Relay domain modules. Real tracked source, byte-identical to the repository's.
#
# NOT a Decision C arm, no readiness credit, lane lab, self-test OFF. The coder cannot run commands, so what it writes is judged by the independent reviewer against the
# acceptance criteria as well as by the seeded specification, which pins the MAIN behaviours of each fix and deliberately not every wider invariant: those are the
# criteria's job. Nothing here forces, injects or counts a reviewer finding: a repair is counted only if the reviewer finds a defect on its own.
#
# THE SLICE: the two modules to fix. Neither has a run-time import (every import is type-only and vanishes under Node's type stripping). Run-time import closure: 2 files.
# The digest module is a hand-written SHA-256 whose only defect is in its UTF-8 encoder; nothing in it is about secrets or capture.
# DELIBERATELY UNPINNED by the seeded specification (the criteria and the reviewer judge them, as in diagnostic 3): collateral change to anything outside the two
# fixes, mutation of inputs, and the rules that `durable-digest.ts` must not gain a `TextEncoder`, a `Buffer` or a `node:` import and that no exported name may be added. The spec also does not test lone surrogates
# inside `stableSerialize`/`digestOf` (only `sha256Hex`), nor sub-millisecond or non-ISO date forms for `evidenceAge`.
